Ingenuous

in-JEN-yoo-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ingenuous is innocently trusting and unsuspecting; open and honest in an unguarded way.

The ingenuous freshman believed every word of the upperclassmen's obvious prank, never suspecting he was being teased.

Worked Example

Her ingenuous excitement about the surprise party made it painfully obvious she had no idea it was already planned.

Being so openly, unsuspectingly excited that it gives away the secret is exactly ingenuous.

How Ingenuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unsuspecting

unsuspecting: not aware of a hidden problem or deception

trustful

trustful: without craftiness or deceit

Antonyms

worldly

worldly: experienced and sophisticated about life

How Strong Is It? — trusting → ingenuous → overtrusting

trusting vs. ingenuous

trusting vs. ingenuous: Trusting simply means willing to believe others -- a common, everyday quality; ingenuous adds a sense of complete, almost childlike innocence behind that trust.

overtrusting vs. ingenuous

overtrusting vs. ingenuous: Overtrusting implies someone is easily and repeatedly fooled, almost to their own detriment, while ingenuous is gentler, describing innocent openness rather than a flaw to be taken advantage of.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: in, into (Latin)

root — genu

root — genu: born, natural (Latin (gignere))

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ingenuous comes from Latin ingenuus ('freeborn, natural') from in- + gignere ('to beget, be born') -- describing someone whose openness feels natural and unlearned.

Use the root in a new word: genuine

Use the root in a new word: genuine: The same gignere root gives us the everyday word genuine -- both words carry the idea of something natural and unforced, rather than staged or fake.

Root Check

Word Choice

Watch this trap: Ingenuous (innocently trusting) is easily confused with the similar-looking Ingenious (cleverly inventive) -- the two words look almost identical but describe nearly opposite qualities, one about innocent openness and the other about sharp cleverness.
